purpose: Convert the rev0373 MA row contract from an empty acquisition contract into a public denial/appeal burden pilot using already-registered MA sources.
why_this_is_riskiest: The cube can otherwise say “we have the sources” while never exposing the quantitative mechanism: many denials are not appealed, many appealed denials are overturned, and public reporting is still too aggregated to prove service-level remedy or harm.
pilot_scope: Public aggregate and service-specific evidence only; no contract-year/service-category row is certified.

public_pilot_records.source_locator: KFF analysis of CMS-submitted MA prior-authorization data, 2024 key takeaways and use-of-prior-authorization section.
public_pilot_records.bounded_inference: A low appeal rate plus high overturn rate makes appeal burden a decisive certification variable; it does not prove which unappealed denials were medically wrong.
noncertification_limits: CMS public reporting is aggregated to contract/insurer level in this analysis
service type and plan-level variation are missing
delay, harm, remedy completion, and clinical correctness are not measured

public_pilot_records.source_locator: HHS-OIG SNF report page, What OIG Found, June 2024 review of 19 MAOs.
public_pilot_records.bounded_inference: For vulnerable post-hospital SNF admissions, appealed denials were overwhelmingly reversed; certification must therefore ask what happened to the much larger unappealed set.
noncertification_limits: single month
19 MAOs only
not all service categories
does not prove each unappealed denial was incorrect
does not measure time-to-care or harm completion for each enrollee

public_pilot_records.source_locator: HHS-OIG LTCH/IRF report page, What OIG Found and recommendations, June 2024 review of 19 MAOs.
public_pilot_records.bounded_inference: Contractor and service-type variation must be a row dimension, not a footnote, because contractors may deny requests later overturned by MAOs.
noncertification_limits: single month
19 MAOs only
not a denominator for all MA services
not a contract-service public row with harm/remedy outcomes

public_pilot_records.source_locator: CY2026 Part C reporting requirements and technical specifications; Parts C/D reporting requirements LDS route.
public_pilot_records.bounded_inference: The required row cannot merely ask for denials; it must preserve request source, service/claim distinction, fully/partially/adverse dispositions, reconsiderations, withdrawn/dismissed records, reopenings, and delegated-entity decisions while naming exclusions such as IRE decisions and some concurrent reviews.
noncertification_limits: architecture is not actual data
LDS access requires DUA/payment and CMS timing
public record may not include the service-level detail OIG says is needed

public_pilot_records.source_locator: CMS-0057-F fact sheet: prior-authorization decision timeframes, specific denial reasons, metrics, APIs, 2026/2027 compliance dates.
public_pilot_records.bounded_inference: Metrics/API rules can become evidence rails, but until actual plan metric rows and API outputs are observed they are remedy infrastructure rather than proof of remedy.
noncertification_limits: future compliance dates
excludes drugs under CMS-0057-F
process metrics may still omit clinical correctness and beneficiary harm

public_pilot_records.source_locator: CMS MA Denial Notice and managed-care notice/form requirements.
public_pilot_records.bounded_inference: A denial notice is a necessary remedy artifact, but the cube must separately measure language/comprehension, appeal initiation, time-to-relief, service furnished, and financial restoration.
noncertification_limits: form route is not delivery proof
does not show comprehension
does not show appeal success or actual care delivered

derived_acceptance_tests.operator_rule: A high overturn rate is not a self-correction pass
derived_acceptance_tests.logic: If appeal_share_of_denials is low and overturn_share_of_appeals is high, the archive must treat appeals as a burden/remedy variable and cannot certify the denial system as self-correcting without unappealed-denial and service-level harm evidence.

If appeal_share_of_denials is low and overturn_share_of_appeals is high, appeal outcomes cannot be read as proof that the denial system self-corrects; unappealed denials, delay, and harm become required rows.
public_values: OIG SNF June 2024: appeal_share 0.18 and overturn_share 0.95

derived_acceptance_tests.logic: If service-specific OIG reports show large variation and contractor-driven denial concern, the row contract must retain service_category, contractor/delegated_entity, and reviewer path.
public_values: OIG LTCH/IRF: LTCH appealed-denial overturn 0.36, IRF appealed-denial overturn 0.43, IRF overturn range 0.14-0.86; contractor concern recorded

derived_acceptance_tests.logic: CY2026 reporting and CMS-0057-F infrastructure identify data rails, but certification still requires actual plan/service rows plus notice/remedy/harm outcomes.
public_values: CMS Part C specs define dispositions and exclusions
CMS Part C/D validation/LDS route has access and timing constraints
CMS-0057-F metrics/API rules have implementation dates

false_pass_blocks: No appeal-overturn pass: high overturn rates increase concern when appeal rates are low.
No aggregate KFF/public-analysis pass: system totals lack service-level harm and remedy rows.
No OIG-service-specific pass: SNF/LTCH/IRF findings are decisive warnings, not complete MA denominators.
No reporting-architecture pass: CMS Part C specs and LDS routes are field maps until rows are acquired.
No API/metric pass: CMS-0057-F is implementation infrastructure until actual metrics/API outputs are joined.
No notice-form pass: appeal rights must be joined to delivery, comprehension, appeal initiation, time-to-relief, and service/payment restoration.
No Star Ratings or quality-context offset for denial/remedy failure.
A high overturn rate is not a self-correction pass when most denials are never appealed.
required_next_rows: one public or LDS contract-year row with request_count, adverse_or_partially_adverse_count, appeal_count, overturn_count, dismissed_or_withdrawn_count, and reopenings
one service-category row distinguishing SNF, LTCH, IRF, inpatient, outpatient, drug, supplemental benefit, or claim/payment service classes
one delegated-entity/contractor row with reviewer and criterion path
one beneficiary remedy row with notice, language, appeal initiation, IRE/reconsideration outcome, time-to-relief, service furnished, and financial restoration
one quality/network/RADV/payment-integrity context row for the same contract-year
operator_rule: A high overturn rate is not a self-correction pass.
bounded_inference_summary: A high overturn rate is not a self-correction pass: with low appeal rates, appeal wins can reveal burden, selection, and access failure rather than effective self-correction.
